text:
olivia: FYI I'm seeing a p99 regression on streaming chat after the mb_autotune tweak last night. p95 stable but p99 up ~220ms. could be MB oscillation + kernel flip on tails.

samir: can you paste the perf trace / a few logs? is this across models or just the medium chat profile?

olivia: only on chat-stream profile (low-latency target). here's the short trace dump, trimmed: 
```
[10:12:34.123] req=0x7f SELECT_KERNEL model=redwood-chat seq_len=16 chunk=stream -> kernel=kv-optimized-v2
[10:12:34.124] req=0x7f KV_CACHE_HIT true
[10:12:34.124] req=0x7f microbatch_size=1 -> executing
[10:12:35.456] req=0x7f kernel_fallback to kernel=generic-cu1 due to small batch
[10:12:35.457] req=0x7f KV_CACHE_SPILL=true memcopy_ms=42
[10:12:35.680] latency_total_ms=620 p99 spike
```
not super long, but you can see a kernel fallback right before the spike and a spill memcopy.

jia: that pattern smells like our hybrid kernel-selection heuristic: when mb drops to 1 the selector switches to generic kernel even though kv cache state expected kv-optimized. oscillation causes >1 fallback per request which triggers memcopies for KV and kills tail.

marco: agreed. the selector currently uses: `if mb_size<=1 then choose generic else choose kv_fast` which is too crude for streaming. we had planned hysteresis but never enabled for streaming path.

olivia: exact. enabling a tiny hysteresis should reduce flip-flopping. also KV spill threshold is low so any fallback triggers spill.

devbot: deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026.03.18-rt-autotune-rc3 queued for eng-runtime/canary.

samir: propose experiments: 3 cohorts, 24h each.
- cohort A: current autotune (baseline)
- cohort B: add mb hysteresis (require change of >=2 to switch)
- cohort C: hysteresis + min_mb enforced at 2 for streaming requests

jia: + measure correlation: p99 vs number_of_kernel_switches and kv_spill_count per request. also track per-token latency, not just request.

marco: small config diff I suggest: 
```json
{"mb_autotune": true, "hysteresis_delta": 2, "min_mb_streaming": 2, "kernel_selection": "pref_kv_when_cache_expected"}
```
we shouldn't hardcode to 2 forever but start there.

ananya: I can run cohorts and dashboards. quick Q: where do I toggle the kv spill logging? need that flag for correlation.

olivia: use /debug/trace?kv=true or add `--kv-spill-log=1` to the runtime args. then the trace lines include KV_CACHE_SPILL and memcopy_ms.

ananya: got it. I'll spin up the canary and run cohort B/C against 5% of traffic each. will capture p95/p99, kernel_switch_rate, kv_spill_rate, and cold_start_rate.

samir: also add a secondary check: p99-token-latency for first token vs subsequent tokens. streaming can hide initial tail.

marco: a note from profiling: when kernel flips we see a ~30-60ms scheduling jitter + memcopy of ~40ms depending on GPU. combined with token post-processing that's our 200-300ms tail. so even small reductions matter.

olivia: good. if cohort C reduces p99 by >100ms and p95 unaffected, we'll roll hysteresis in mainline.

devbot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started: 2026.03.18-rt-autotune-rc3 -> eng-runtime/canary (5% B, 5% C).

ananya: running now. initial sanity after 5k samples: baseline p99=590ms, cohort B p99=520ms, cohort C p99=485ms. kv_spill_rate baseline=0.7%, B=0.45%, C=0.22%. kernel_switches/request baseline=0.09, B=0.03, C=0.01.

jia: that's promising. can you paste the burndown of p99 vs time? also any edge cases (long sequences) where min_mb=2 hurts throughput?

ananya: throughput hit measured: tail throughput down ~0.8% for cohort C, within SLA. long sequences (>512) not affected. small samples show some slight increase in small-request latency median (+10ms) but p99 wins.

olivia: ok let's hold for 24h but this looks safe. thanks team. I'll draft a small runtime change (enable hysteresis and min_mb_streaming=2 behind toggle) and we can ship after full run.

marco: one more: we should add a kernel-selector metric: `kernel_selected` and `kernel_switch_count` per request to make future debugging easier.

samir: + alert: set p99 > 600ms for streaming chat to page eng-oncall during rollout.

olivia: noted, filing rollout PR and will include metric + alert.

opsbot: incident-watch: created ticket #RT-8234 for rollout tracking.

ananya: will post final numbers in ~22h.

olivia: thanks, closing loop later. :thumbsup:
